label: Employee
description: Least-privilege baseline for a plain employee: read the org catalogues and colleagues' directory records, act on your own records, work the shared boards. Nothing here reaches another person's PII, pay or HR-only fields.
relies_on: The `everyone` pseudo-role rules (roles/everyone.json): the app shell every account needs (own user record, own preferences, own operations, the batch transport), own notifications (list, read, write, markAllRead) and the assets the caller holds (list, acknowledge). They union into every caller, so they are not repeated here.
Per-object ACL shares for org documents. This role has no org-documents access; each policy an employee must read and sign arrives as a share on that document.

excluded.why: Wildcard verb on own tickets let a requester assign, route, prioritize, start, resolve and triage their own ticket; the ticket service does not block the requester from those. Replaced by the requester verbs named above.
The ticket checklist is the servicing agent's work list.
Routing suggestions are for the help desk, not the requester.
As a verb allow this also grants every card verb added later. The current verbs are named instead, so a new one is withheld until someone grants it.

Would reach private boards (`vp-`), which are seen only by the people and roles they are shared with, their creator and their department's managers (services/boardShares.ts). The two org-visible segments are named instead.

excluded.pattern: boards | cards | sprints .me | my-dept | my-reports | my-org .**
excluded.why: These tokens match by code, and boards, cards and sprints are coded by BOARD (domain/boardAccess.ts): a board-coded row is nobody's employee or department code, and a two-character board segment can spell a department's code. Held by no role.

The acknowledge service does not check the caller can read the document, and signing files a copy of the policy PDF to the signer. A role-wide grant would leak any requires-ack policy by id. It must come with each document's share.
Per-record activity trail is private by default; grant per role or record in the ACL.
Org documents are private by default; each is shared individually.
Colleagues' presence pills are derived from their leave and attendance, which a plain employee does not read. Managers hold it for their department, HR for everyone.
HR's: reconciling a pending vendor e-sign, and printing a letter on its letterhead. The Documents page offers both only to those who can edit the document.
The board and the suggestion box are the everyone role's, so every account reaches them whatever its role (roles/everyone.json).
